rules.name: The default invalidation level is the protected swing that should hold if the thesis is correct
rules.setupAnchor: After a protected low or protected high is confirmed, use that swing as the structural line the market must defend
rules.confirmationTrigger: Bullish setups stay valid while the protected low holds; bearish setups stay valid while the protected high holds
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: A protected swing becomes the active invalidation anchor only after price reaches an important level and closes through the candle series that created the move into that level
rules.invalidationCondition: Price trades beyond the protected swing that was supposed to hold for the active thesis
rules.targetLogic: Place the stop beyond the protected swing and keep the trade thesis active only while that structural anchor remains intact
exceptions: Do not assign invalidation to an anticipated swing before the required confirming close has actually printed
machineChecks: Require a confirmed protected swing before declaring the invalidation level
Place bullish invalidation below the protected low and bearish invalidation above the protected high
Flip the thesis to invalid once price breaches the active protected swing

rules.name: Body-based invalidation is an optional risk-tightening variant, not the default structural rule
rules.setupAnchor: Start from the default protected swing invalidation, then consider moving the stop to the body of the swing candle only when structure justifies tighter risk
rules.confirmationTrigger: Use body invalidation only when the swing candle is supported by large bulk opposing candles rather than large rejection wicks
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The protected swing remains the true structural anchor even when the chosen stop is tightened to the body for risk-to-reward reasons
rules.invalidationCondition: Price closes or trades through the chosen body-based invalidation level before the trade reaches its objective
rules.targetLogic: Use body invalidation to improve risk-to-reward on nearby objectives, knowing that the trade can be stopped before the full structural thesis is actually broken
exceptions: Do not use body invalidation on large-wicked opposing candles
When structure is wick-dominated, revert to the full protected swing invalidation
machineChecks: Treat protected swing invalidation as the default rule and body invalidation as an optional override
Reject body invalidation when the swing candle is dominated by large rejection wicks
Mark body invalidation setups as tighter-risk variants rather than structurally stronger setups
ambiguityNotes: The first machine-checkable definition of big bulk opposing candles versus large wicked opposing candles still needs a stricter algorithm

rules.name: If the initial reversal invalidation is too wide, wait for the next protected swing instead of forcing the trade
rules.setupAnchor: After the first reversal-level protected swing appears, compare its structural invalidation distance against the available target
rules.confirmationTrigger: If the initial protected swing produces poor risk-to-reward, defer entry and wait for a new protected swing to form in the same direction after retracement or continuation structure develops
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Later protected swings in the same thesis can tighten invalidation while preserving the original directional idea
rules.invalidationCondition: A later protected swing never forms, or price invalidates the original thesis before a tighter continuation-style entry develops
rules.targetLogic: Improve risk-to-reward by entering from later structure rather than compressing the original stop in a way that ignores invalidation logic
exceptions: This is a patience filter, not a requirement to re-enter endlessly after every missed move
machineChecks: Compare the initial invalidation distance with the available target distance
Allow the setup to defer rather than force a trade when the initial stop is too wide for the objective
Promote the deferred setup only when a later protected swing forms in the same direction
ambiguityNotes: The minimum acceptable reward-to-risk threshold for when a trade should be deferred instead of taken is not yet numeric

rules.name: A setup is invalid when structure loses intent through consolidation, target completion, or failed directional follow-through
rules.setupAnchor: After a continuation or reversal setup becomes active, monitor whether price shows decisive follow-through or instead drifts into range behavior or reaches the higher-timeframe objective
rules.confirmationTrigger: Keep the setup active only while price remains fast, decisive, and structurally aligned with the original thesis
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: Protected swings should lead to clean continuation or reversal expression; if price overlaps, grinds sideways, or finishes the main objective, the original setup quality is gone
rules.invalidationCondition: Price turns into consolidation instead of expanding, sweeps the relevant objective and stalls, or trades back through the range in a way that breaks the original directional read
rules.targetLogic: Cancel or avoid re-entry once the higher-timeframe objective has been met or the intended structure has degraded into a range or opposing move
exceptions: A setup can stay contextually valid after a pause, but not as the same immediate entry once structure has clearly turned into consolidation
machineChecks: Invalidate continuation or reversal setups when price resolves into a consolidation rather than immediate directional follow-through
Reject fresh entries after the higher-timeframe objective has already been met
Mark the original thesis as failed when price rotates back through the range and destroys the expected directional structure
ambiguityNotes: The first strict timing rule for when hesitation becomes consolidation-invalidation instead of acceptable pause still needs a stricter algorithm
